Status

FinKore Core 2.0.5 stable.

Purpose

This document defines Transition Guards: domain predicates that control whether a declared Transition may occur.

Requirements

  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-001 — A Transition Guard MUST evaluate against the facts provided for the Transition Request.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    A proof can establish a property different from the intended rule ↗

    Florin Stoica; Laura Florentina Stoica

    A translated property must still describe the applicable guards and intended observation. Requirement references aid review but do not prove translation equivalence. The source’s reported assistant error does not mandate ATL/APEX or measure a general LLM error rate.

    Scope and limitations

    A changed ordering example is reviewer inference; the source reports a particular assistant/model interaction. No general LLM error rate or superiority of a prompting strategy is established here. Formulas and figures were not independently inspected visually.

  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-002 — Every applicable Transition Guard MUST pass before the Transition succeeds.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    A proof can establish a property different from the intended rule ↗

    A translated property must still describe the applicable guards and intended observation. Requirement references aid review but do not prove translation equivalence. The source’s reported assistant error does not mandate ATL/APEX or measure a general LLM error rate.

  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-003 — Transition Guard evaluation MUST NOT change Workflow State or other domain data.
  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 — A Transition Guard result MUST be deterministic for the same declared facts, or the guard definition MUST identify its dependence on external facts.
    Evidence & context3 research notes · 1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Illustrates a risk

    Fast responses do not establish that the relevant facts are current ↗

    Ruth Octaviani P. Wermasubun; Linjte Kalangi; Heince R. N. Wokas

    Explicit dependencies and comparisons against supplied observations do not guarantee freshness of remote facts. The reported synchronization issue motivates a conditional application risk, not a Core age limit.

    Scope and limitations

    The source reports synchronization issues, not a measured stale-snapshot control failure. The financial scenario in the original finding is reviewer-created. Historical reports may intentionally use old observations.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    A changed prediction is a changed fact basis, not necessarily nondeterministic condition evaluation ↗

    Bingying Jiang; Jialei Cao; Yutong Tan; Shi Qiu

    Deterministic evaluation concerns the declared fact basis. A changed prediction changes that basis; the source does not demonstrate a FinKore violation or prohibit adaptive models.

    Scope and limitations

    Reviewer scenario: a later model recomputes a different risk estimate; this does not reproduce the earlier supplied estimate. Whether that estimate is material and retained depends on the declared policy.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Snapshot coherence and freshness are separate properties ↗

    Dan R. K. Ports; Austin T. Clements; Irene Zhang; Samuel Madden; Barbara Liskov

    Explicit context and supplied-observation checks do not certify a coherent or sufficiently recent remote snapshot. The cache source distinguishes coherence from age; acceptable age and isolation remain composing-application choices.

    Scope and limitations

    These financial scenarios are reviewer inferences. A consistent snapshot can be appropriate within an application’s bound. TxCache does not remove the database’s anomalies or establish universal safe staleness for financial authorization.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    Batch dependencies expose a distinction between reproducible facts and fresh facts ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    A guard is deterministic for the same declared facts or identifies external dependencies. Retain the published PARTIAL coverage note.

    Scope and limitations

    The source supplies no quantitative freshness bound or dependency protocol. WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 does not require always-latest data; ENTITY-IMPORT-007 compares expected values to the supplied observation, not to an independently queried remote system. The interview's suggestion that real-time processing removes these problems is not generalized: distributed real-time systems still require dependency and freshness policies.

  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-005 — Authorization MAY be an input to a guard, but a guard MUST NOT assume a particular authorization model.
  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-006 — Guard evaluation order MUST NOT change the logical result when all guards evaluate the same supplied facts.
  • WORKFLOW-GUARD-007 — An implementation retaining native comparison values in a declared guard MUST document its supported value set, capture independently owned containers, and retain only supported immutable scalar values. Unsupported or mutable numeric objects, including unsupported subclasses of supported numeric classes, MUST fail definition construction/import with FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEFINITION before they can alter retained semantics. Supported exact numeric values MUST be preserved without conversion through binary floating point or arbitrary numeric string coercion. Failure MUST leave existing instances and their bindings unchanged, and MUST follow WORKFLOW-ERROR-007's definition-first priority.

WORKFLOW-GUARD-007 preserves WORKFLOW-VERSION-003/009's ownership guarantee and WORKFLOW-GUARD-004's determinism. The conformance guard is a top-level own-member comparison; Approval's nested selectors do not change it. Conformance conventions define that fixture. Implementations document their native supported-value profiles; no universal serializer or production guard language is required.

Invariants

Failure of any required Transition Guard must leave current State unchanged. Guard order must not change the logical result when all guards are evaluated against the same facts.

External dependency declarations (Non-Normative)

WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 places an existing obligation on the guard definition: evaluation is deterministic for the same declared facts, or the definition identifies its dependence on external facts. CoreDoc CORE-005.3 also identifies relevant context and external dependencies as part of an evaluation's stated basis. Declaring a dependency does not make hidden changes to that basis reproducible or permit guard evaluation to mutate domain data.

For example, an application can supply a Boolean indicating that its processing window is open, or that an external eligibility check passed. The guard can compare that supplied value without consulting a clock or provider. How the application obtained the value is a separate dependency: a definition that instead relies on a live clock or eligibility source identifies that reliance. An equal Boolean alone does not establish the same source observation or evaluation context.

Declarations remain consumer-authored under the current contract. Review can ask which guard and definition binding depend on which external facts, how those facts affect the result, and which supplied values and context explain the evaluation. Source references, observation times, or retained snapshots can help where the application's policy makes them relevant. These are review prompts, not new required members, claim fields, a retention regime, or a standardized provenance model.

A portable schema for external-dependency declarations, its omission/null rules, and errors for malformed declarations are not published: This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. The local fact-equality fixture is not that schema. Its existing definition-validation errors do not establish new failures for an unspecified declaration format.

Traceability therefore keeps WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 PARTIAL. Consumer declaration review and native ownership evidence address their existing boundaries; neither supplies the missing portable authoring representation. This limitation does not waive the dependency obligation or change current transition results, errors, or failure atomicity. No provider, callback interface, authorization model, or production guard language is selected here.

Examples

Transition: SUBMITTED → APPROVED
Guard: required approvals are satisfied

Invalid Examples

  • Changing entity data as an undocumented side effect of evaluating a guard.
  • Allowing a transition after a required guard fails.

Errors

A Transition Guard rejection must report FINKORE_WORKFLOW_GUARD_REJECTED. A composing domain may provide additional context or a secondary domain code without replacing this failure category.

Open Questions

  • How should time-sensitive or externally sourced facts be captured for reproducible evaluation?
